name: generic_fadvise
prose: Precondition: file is a valid open struct file with an inode; offset, len and advice are caller-supplied. Postcondition: returns -ESPIPE if the inode is a FIFO, before anything else is touched. Returns -EINVAL if file->f_mapping is NULL or len is negative, again without side effects. If the inode is DAX or the backing_dev_info is noop_backing_dev_info, the advice is not applied: it returns 0 when advice is one of POSIX_FADV_NORMAL, RANDOM, SEQUENTIAL, WILLNEED, NOREUSE or DONTNEED and -EINVAL for any other value. Otherwise the end byte is offset+len minus 1 (computed in unsigned arithmetic; len == 0 or an overflowing sum means up to LLONG_MAX), and the advice is handled: NORMAL sets file->f_ra.ra_pages to bdi->ra_pages and clears FMODE_RANDOM and FMODE_NOREUSE in f_mode (under f_lock); RANDOM sets FMODE_RANDOM; SEQUENTIAL sets ra_pages to twice bdi->ra_pages and clears FMODE_RANDOM; NOREUSE sets FMODE_NOREUSE; WILLNEED calls force_page_cache_readahead over the page range covering the offset..end byte (a page count of 0 after wraparound becomes ~0UL) and leaves f_mode and ra_pages alone; DONTNEED starts non-blocking writeback (WB_SYNC_NONE) of the byte range, then invalidates only pages lying completely inside the range (with lru_add_drain, and a second invalidate pass after lru_add_drain_all when some pages could not be invalidated), and does nothing more when the end page index would be 0 or lies before the first full page. Any other advice value returns -EINVAL. The remaining paths return 0. f_lock is taken and released inside the function; no locks, references or memory are passed to the caller.
note: Reviewers right on all 3 points: DAX/noop branch returns -EINVAL for unknown advice (fadvise.c:61-62); len==0 means up to LLONG_MAX (72-74); DONTNEED/WILLNEED do not touch f_mode/ra_pages (96-107, 113-172).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(fadvise64_64, int, fd, loff_t, offset, loff_t, len, int, advice)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_fadvise64_64 (entry point sys_fadvise64_64 / __x64_sys_fadvise64_64 on x86-64), compiled only when CONFIG_ADVISE_SYSCALLS is set. Its body is a single call: it returns ksys_fadvise64_64(fd, offset, len, advice). ksys_fadvise64_64 looks up fd with CLASS(fd, f) (the reference is released when the scope exits), returns -EBADF if the descriptor is empty, and otherwise returns vfs_fadvise(fd_file(f), offset, len, advice). vfs_fadvise calls file->f_op->fadvise when the file operations define it and generic_fadvise otherwise, so the result is whatever that callee returns (0 or a negative errno).
note: Name changed to the macro head as in the file (fadvise.c:201). Old prose attributed the fd lookup to this function; it is in ksys_fadvise64_64 (191-199).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(fadvise64, int, fd, loff_t, offset, size_t, len, int, advice)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_fadvise64 (entry point sys_fadvise64 / __x64_sys_fadvise64 on x86-64), compiled only when CONFIG_ADVISE_SYSCALLS and __ARCH_WANT_SYS_FADVISE64 are set. len is a size_t, and its body is one call: it returns ksys_fadvise64_64(fd, offset, len, advice) with len converted to loff_t. ksys_fadvise64_64 returns -EBADF if fd does not resolve to an open file and otherwise returns vfs_fadvise(...), which calls the file's f_op->fadvise when present and generic_fadvise otherwise; the result is 0 or a negative errno from that callee. The descriptor lookup reference is released when ksys_fadvise64_64 returns.
note: Name changed to the macro head (fadvise.c:208). fd lookup lives in ksys_fadvise64_64, not in the syscall body.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE6(fadvise64_64, int, fd, compat_arg_u64_dual(offset), compat_arg_u64_dual(len), int, advice)
prose: Generated compat function (entry point compat_sys_fadvise64_64 / __x64_compat_sys_fadvise64_64 on x86-64), compiled only when CONFIG_ADVISE_SYSCALLS, CONFIG_COMPAT and __ARCH_WANT_COMPAT_FADVISE64_64 are set. The 64-bit offset and len are passed as register pairs and rebuilt with compat_arg_u64_glue; the body returns ksys_fadvise64_64(fd, glued offset, glued len, advice). ksys_fadvise64_64 returns -EBADF if fd is not an open descriptor and otherwise returns vfs_fadvise(...), i.e. f_op->fadvise if defined or generic_fadvise, giving 0 or a negative errno. The descriptor lookup reference is released when ksys_fadvise64_64 returns.
note: Name changed to the macro head (fadvise.c:217-218).

name: failslab_debugfs_init
prose: Static __init function registered with late_initcall when CONFIG_FAULT_INJECTION_DEBUG_FS is set. It calls fault_create_debugfs_attr("failslab", NULL, &failslab.attr); if that returns an error pointer, it returns PTR_ERR of it and creates nothing else. Otherwise it calls debugfs_create_bool for "ignore-gfp-wait" (bound to failslab.ignore_gfp_reclaim) and "cache-filter" (bound to failslab.cache_filter), both with mode S_IFREG|0600 under the returned directory, and returns 0. debugfs_create_bool returns void, so a failure to create either file is not detected and does not change the return value.
note: Reviewer 1 right (no guarantee entries exist; return is 0 regardless, failslab.c:66-71). Reviewer 2 refers to a contract that is now empty.

name: generic_perform_write
prose: Precondition: iocb->ki_filp has a mapping whose a_ops provide write_begin and write_end, and iov_iter i describes the data; the caller is expected to hold the inode lock. Behaviour: the chunk size starts at mapping_max_folio_size and the function loops while iov_iter_count(i) is non-zero. Each pass calls balance_dirty_pages_ratelimited, breaks with status -EINTR if a fatal signal is pending, calls ->write_begin (a negative status breaks out of the loop), copies with copy_folio_from_iter_atomic, then calls ->write_end. When write_end returns a status different from copied, i is reverted by copied minus max(status, 0) bytes; a negative status then breaks out of the loop. A positive status advances pos and the written count by status. A status of 0 halves the chunk size when it is above PAGE_SIZE; if copied is non-zero it retries the same chunk with bytes = copied (the iterator was reverted), and if copied is zero it calls fault_in_iov_iter_readable and, when nothing at all could be faulted in, sets -EFAULT and breaks, otherwise the loop continues. Return: if no bytes were written it returns the last status value, which on the paths that leave the loop is -EINTR, a negative errno from ->write_begin or ->write_end, or -EFAULT. Otherwise it adds the written count to iocb->ki_pos and returns that count, even if the loop ended on an error after a partial write. The iterator is left advanced by exactly the bytes counted as written.
note: Reviewer 1 right (retry only if copied>0, else fault-in path, 4309-4324). Reviewer 2 half right: no-write return is a negative status, never 0 on the traced paths. Reviewer 3 wrong: a zero-length iterator goes through one pass, write_end returns 0, fault_in_iov_iter_readable(i,0)==0==bytes so status becomes -EFAULT (4321-4323), not 0 (assuming write_begin succeeds).

name: hmm_dma_map_pfn
prose: Precondition: dev, map and p2pdma_state are valid; idx is a valid index into map->pfn_list (and into map->dma_list when dma_need_unmap(dev) is true and the IOVA path is not used); pfns[idx] describes a page; the caller serializes access to map. Early return: if pfns[idx] has HMM_PFN_DMA_MAPPED and not HMM_PFN_P2PDMA_BUS, then under dma_use_iova(state) it returns state->addr + idx*dma_entry_size, else when dma_need_unmap(dev) it returns dma_addrs[idx], in both cases without changing pfns[idx]; if neither holds it falls through and maps again. Otherwise it switches on pci_p2pdma_state: NONE continues; THRU_HOST_BRIDGE adds DMA_ATTR_MMIO and sets HMM_PFN_P2PDMA in pfns[idx]; BUS_ADDR sets HMM_PFN_P2PDMA_BUS and HMM_PFN_DMA_MAPPED and returns the result of pci_p2pdma_bus_addr_map without mapping anything; any other value returns DMA_MAPPING_ERROR with pfns[idx] unchanged. Mapping: with dma_use_iova it calls dma_iova_link, then dma_iova_sync, and if the sync fails it calls dma_iova_unlink for that range first; the address is state->addr + offset. Without IOVA it fails if WARN_ON_ONCE(dma_need_unmap(dev) && !dma_addrs) fires, else calls dma_map_phys and, on success with dma_need_unmap(dev), records the address in dma_addrs[idx]. On success it sets HMM_PFN_DMA_MAPPED and returns the DMA address. On dma_iova_link failure, dma_iova_sync failure (after the unlink), the WARN_ON_ONCE case or dma_map_phys failure it clears HMM_PFN_P2PDMA in pfns[idx] and returns DMA_MAPPING_ERROR; the other flags are left as they were.
note: Reviewer 1 right that the default case and the BUS_ADDR case do not clear HMM_PFN_P2PDMA (hmm.c:812-816 vs error label 848-850); old prose lumped them in with the clearing cases. Reviewer 2: the old prose already said unlink happens (828), and the sync-failure path is as described; code unlinks before error.

name: __folio_split
prose: Static function __folio_split(folio, new_order, split_at, lock_at, list, uniform_split) in mm/huge_memory.c (the slice starts in the middle of its body). Precondition: folio is a locked large folio, and the caller holds a reference on it; split_at and lock_at must be pages of folio. Early failures: -EINVAL if split_at or lock_at is not in folio, or if new_order >= the current order; a non-zero result of folio_check_splittable is returned (-EINVAL, -EBUSY etc.); these paths skip the memcg switch. Otherwise it makes the folio's memcg the active memcg and: for anonymous folios gets the anon_vma (-EBUSY if there is none) and write-locks it; for file folios returns -EINVAL if new_order is below the mapping's minimum folio order, -EBUSY if filemap_release_folio fails, the xarray error if xas_split_alloc fails for a uniform split, else takes i_mmap_lock_read and notes the end index from i_size. It then returns -EAGAIN if the folio has unexpected references (racy check), unmaps the folio, and with interrupts disabled and the xarray locked (file folios) returns -EAGAIN if the folio is no longer at its page-cache slot. It takes the deferred-split queue lock and tries folio_ref_freeze; if the freeze fails it returns -EAGAIN. On success of the freeze it removes the folio from the deferred list, adjusts THP counters, rejects a swapcache folio that also has a mapping with -EINVAL, calls __split_unmapped_folio and uses its return value as the result (it can be -ENOMEM with the folio only partly split), unfreezes the new folios and puts them on the LRU or the given list, stores them into the page cache or swap cache, drops folios beyond EOF, then unfreezes the original folio. Cleanup on all paths after the unmap: re-enables interrupts, uncharges dropped shmem pages, calls remap_page, drops i_mmap_lock, unlocks every resulting folio except the one containing lock_at (and frees those through free_folio_and_swap_cache), unlocks and puts the anon_vma, restores the active memcg and drops the memcg reference, destroys the xas, and updates the split / split-failed event counters. The return value is 0 on success or the negative errno described above; the folio containing lock_at stays locked for the caller.
note: Slice cut the head: real function is __folio_split (huge_memory.c:3735, slice starts at 3828); old prose described only the success shape and listed -EAGAIN/-EINVAL only, missing -EBUSY, -ENOMEM from __split_unmapped_folio, and xas errors.

name: anon_enabled_store
prose: Sysfs store handler for a thpsize kobject's anon enabled attribute. It takes order from to_thpsize(kobj)->order and starts with ret = count. If buf matches (sysfs_streq) "always", "inherit", "madvise" or "never", then under huge_anon_orders_lock it sets the bit for order in the matching huge_anon_orders_* bitmap (none for "never") and clears the bits for order in the other bitmaps, then releases the lock. If buf matches none of the four strings, ret is -EINVAL and no bitmap is touched. Afterwards, if ret is greater than 0 it calls start_stop_khugepaged() and, if that returns a non-zero error, returns that error instead (the bitmaps have already been changed). So the result is count on a successful match with count > 0, the error from start_stop_khugepaged, 0 when buf matched but count is 0 (start_stop_khugepaged is not called), or -EINVAL when nothing matched, including when count is 0.
note: Reviewer 1 right (error from start_stop_khugepaged after bits changed, huge_memory.c:612-614). Reviewer 2 (round 15) right: with count==0 and non-matching buf ret=-EINVAL (606-607); old prose said 0 'if count == 0' unconditionally.

name: __vma_reservation_common
prose: Static function __vma_reservation_common(h, vma, addr, mode) returning long. If vma has no resv_map (vma_resv_map returns NULL) it returns 1 without touching any map. Otherwise it computes idx = vma_hugecache_offset(h, vma, addr) and works on the one-page range [idx, idx+1) of the resv_map, by mode: VMA_NEEDS_RESV: ret = region_chg(...); VM_BUG_ON fires if the number of regions needed is not 1. VMA_COMMIT_RESV: ret = region_add; VM_BUG_ON if ret < 0. VMA_END_RESV: region_abort, ret = 0. VMA_ADD_RESV: for a VM_MAYSHARE vma ret = region_add (VM_BUG_ON if negative); otherwise region_abort then ret = region_del. VMA_DEL_RESV: for a VM_MAYSHARE vma region_abort then ret = region_del; otherwise ret = region_add (VM_BUG_ON if negative). Any other mode calls BUG(). Return value: ret as computed if the vma is VM_MAYSHARE or mode is VMA_DEL_RESV; otherwise (private vma, any other mode) the sense is inverted: 0 if ret > 0, 1 if ret == 0, and ret itself if ret < 0. The function takes no lock of its own; the region_* helpers take resv_map->lock.
note: Reviewer 1 right in the old prose-version, and the current prose already had it (private VMA_DEL_RESV returns ret, hugetlb.c:2645-2646). Reviewer 2: old precondition text about hugetlb_lock is not in the code; locking is inside region_* helpers. VM_BUG_ON only checks under CONFIG_DEBUG_VM; wording kept as 'fires'.

name: region_chg
prose: Static function region_chg(resv, f, t, out_regions_needed) on a struct resv_map. It takes resv->lock, calls add_reservation_in_range(resv, f, t, NULL, NULL, out_regions_needed) to count the huge pages in [f, t) not yet in the map (chg) and the regions needed, and sets *out_regions_needed to 1 if that count came back 0. It then calls allocate_file_region_entries(resv, *out_regions_needed); that helper drops resv->lock while allocating and re-takes it only when the allocation loop completes. If the helper fails it returns -ENOMEM: the helper has already released resv->lock on that path and region_chg does not take it again, so the lock is not held on return, adds_in_progress is unchanged, and *out_regions_needed has already been set. Otherwise it adds *out_regions_needed to resv->adds_in_progress, releases resv->lock and returns chg.
note: All three reviewer claims (lock still held on -ENOMEM) are wrong: allocate_file_region_entries does spin_unlock at hugetlb.c:709 and its out_of_memory path (725-730) returns -ENOMEM without re-locking, so region_chg's early return at 831-832 leaves the lock released. The packet prose was right; tightened wording only.

name: need_mlock_drain
prose: Static inline stub for !CONFIG_MMU builds in mm/internal.h: takes a cpu number and returns false, with no other effect. When CONFIG_MMU is set, internal.h only declares need_mlock_drain(int cpu) and the real definition is in mm/mlock.c, so this description applies to the stub only.
note: Reviewer right that the old prose 'always returns false' did not hold for the CONFIG_MMU declaration (internal.h:1063); the definition in this slice is the !CONFIG_MMU stub at internal.h:1153, so it is kept (not dropped) with the scope stated.

name: collapse_huge_page
prose: Static function collapse_huge_page(mm, address, referenced, unmapped, cc) in khugepaged.c. Precondition: address is HPAGE_PMD_SIZE-aligned (VM_BUG_ON checks it) and the caller holds mmap_lock for read on entry. It releases the read lock first, calls alloc_charge_folio (on failure the folio pointer is NULL and the result is that function's error), then re-takes the read lock and runs hugepage_vma_revalidate and find_pmd_or_thp_or_none, dropping the read lock and failing on any non-SCAN_SUCCEED result. If unmapped is set it calls __collapse_huge_page_swapin, which releases mmap_lock itself when it fails. It then drops the read lock, takes mmap_lock for write, re-validates the vma and checks the pmd (failing with the write lock released if either fails), write-locks the anon_vma, clears the PMD with pmdp_collapse_flush, and maps the page table with pte_offset_map_lock (SCAN_PMD_NULL if that fails). __collapse_huge_page_isolate runs next; if it fails (or the pte map failed) the original page table is put back with pmd_populate and the anon_vma lock released. After a successful isolate it calls __collapse_huge_page_copy; if that returns non-success (SCAN_COPY_MC) the copy helper itself restores the original page table with pmd_populate and releases the isolated pages. On success it marks the folio uptodate, installs a huge PMD (rmap, LRU, deposit of the old page table, set_pmd_at, deferred split registration) and sets folio to NULL, because the mapping consumes the allocation reference; the result is SCAN_SUCCEED. On every return, success or failure, mmap_lock is not held by the caller afterwards. A non-NULL folio left on a failure path is released with folio_put. The return value is SCAN_SUCCEED or the failing step's SCAN_* code.
note: All three reviewer claims right: early failures leave the PMD alone and folio NULL (khugepaged.c:1107-1122); swapin failure releases mmap_lock inside the callee (1124-1133); copy failure restores the pagetable inside __collapse_huge_page_copy_failed via pmd_populate (khugepaged.c:749-750), so the old 'copy failure leaves it empty' was wrong.

name: collapse_file
prose: Static function collapse_file(mm, addr, file, start, cc), which tries to replace the page-cache folios of file in [start, start+HPAGE_PMD_NR) by one huge folio. Preconditions (VM_BUG_ON): start is HPAGE_PMD_NR-aligned, and either CONFIG_READ_ONLY_THP_FOR_FS is set or file is shmem. It first calls alloc_charge_folio; if that fails it returns its error code (SCAN_ALLOC_HUGE_PAGE_FAIL or SCAN_CGROUP_CHARGE_FAIL) with nothing else changed. Otherwise it locks the new folio, creates the xarray slots (SCAN_FAIL if they cannot be created), and walks the range, locking and isolating each existing folio from the LRU. Failures in this walk give: SCAN_TRUNCATED (range empty for shmem, or folio no longer in this mapping), SCAN_PAGE_LOCK (trylock failed), SCAN_FAIL (shmem_get_folio or filemap_lock_folio failed, folio not uptodate, non-shmem folio dirty or under writeback), SCAN_PTE_MAPPED_HUGEPAGE (a PMD-order folio already sits at start), SCAN_DEL_PAGE_LRU, SCAN_PAGE_HAS_PRIVATE, SCAN_PAGE_COUNT (unexpected reference count). For non-shmem files without large-folio support it increments nr_thps and gives SCAN_FAIL if the inode is open for write or writeback fails; shmem holes are charged with shmem_charge (SCAN_FAIL on failure). The data is then copied or zeroed into the new folio, with SCAN_COPY_MC on a machine-check copy failure. If there were holes, the empty slots are checked with retry entries: SCAN_STORE_FAILED (store error), SCAN_PAGE_FILLED (a hole was filled meanwhile), SCAN_EXCEED_NONE_PTE (a vma with userfaultfd missing mode overlaps). On success the new folio is marked uptodate, added to the LRU and stored in the page cache as one multi-index entry, page tables are retracted, the new folio is unlocked and the old folios are unlocked and released; the result is SCAN_SUCCEED, except that when cc is non-NULL and !cc->is_khugepaged the success result is changed to SCAN_PTE_MAPPED_HUGEPAGE. The caller therefore cannot tell from the value alone whether SCAN_PTE_MAPPED_HUGEPAGE means that case or the existing-huge-folio failure above. On failure (any result other than those success cases) the isolated folios are unlocked and returned to the LRU, the hole accounting is undone where it had been applied, the nr_thps increment is undone for SCAN_COPY_MC on non-shmem files, and the new folio has its mapping cleared, is unlocked and freed.
note: Reviewer 1 (new folio unlocked on success) right, current prose already says unlocked (khugepaged.c:2189 folio_unlock). Reviewer 2 (SCAN_PAGE_FILLED) already covered, path at 2167-2169. Reviewer 3 partly right: SCAN_PTE_MAPPED_HUGEPAGE is returned both for an existing THP (2005, failure) and for MADV_COLLAPSE success (2191-2192); prose rewritten to say both.

name: __msan_chain_origin
prose: KMSAN instrumentation entry point __msan_chain_origin(origin), declared and then defined in mm/kmsan/instrumentation.c. It starts with ret = 0. If kmsan_enabled is false or kmsan_in_runtime() is true, it returns 0 immediately, without saving the user-access flags and without entering the runtime. Otherwise it saves the user-access flags (user_access_save), enters the KMSAN runtime, sets ret = kmsan_internal_chain_origin(origin), leaves the runtime, restores the saved flags and returns ret, whatever kmsan_internal_chain_origin produced. It takes no caller-visible lock or reference.
note: No reviewer claim left to check beyond the old contract (now empty). Prose matches instrumentation.c:240-256.

name: stable_tree_search
prose: Static function stable_tree_search(page) in mm/ksm.c; the packet slice started after its head. It returns a struct folio pointer, ERR_PTR(-EBUSY) or NULL. If the page's folio already has a stable node whose head is not migrate_nodes (a forked KSM page), it takes a folio reference and returns the folio at once. Otherwise it searches the stable tree for the folio's NUMA node, calling cond_resched on each step and calling chain_prune; if chain_prune returns NULL (stale node) the search restarts from the root. On a content match: - if the page has its own stable node (page_node) and the folio mapcount is above 1, it goes to chain_append; - if the matched dup is not a page-sharing candidate it returns NULL; - otherwise it calls ksm_get_folio with trylock: -EBUSY is returned as ERR_PTR(-EBUSY), a NULL result restarts the search, otherwise the folio is unlocked and, if the dup's node still matches its pfn's nid, the tree folio is returned still holding the reference taken by ksm_get_folio (the caller must drop it); if the nid no longer matches the reference is dropped and the replace path runs. If no match is found it returns NULL when page_node is NULL; otherwise it removes page_node from its list, inserts it into the tree and goes to out, which takes a folio reference and returns the page's own folio if page_node is a page-sharing candidate, else NULL. Replace path (matched dup on the wrong NUMA node): without a chain, page_node (if any) replaces the dup in the rbtree, otherwise the dup is erased; with a chain the dup is deleted from the chain and page_node (if any) is added to the chain. The page's folio is returned with a new reference only when page_node exists and is a sharing candidate, else NULL. In both sub-cases the old dup is put on the migrate_nodes list. chain_append path: if there was no chain, alloc_stable_node_chain creates one (NULL is returned if it fails, leaving page_node on migrate_nodes); then page_node is added to the chain and out is taken as above. This path does not move the matched dup to migrate_nodes.
note: Slice cut the head (stable_tree_search at ksm.c:1798, slice starts 1808). Reviewer 15 right: chain_append does not touch stable_node_dup->head / list (ksm.c:1974-2002); only the replace path does at 1970-1971.

name: memblock_cap_memory_range
prose: __init function memblock_cap_memory_range(base, size). It returns without doing anything in three cases: size is 0 (silently), memblock_memory->total_size is 0 (it prints a warning "No memory registered yet" only in this case), or memblock_isolate_range on memblock.memory for [base, base+size) returns non-zero (nothing is removed in that case). Otherwise, after isolating the range into its own regions (which may split regions at base and base+size), it removes every memory region with index at or above the end of the isolated range and every region below its start, except regions marked MEMBLOCK_NOMAP, which are kept. It then removes the reserved ranges [0, base) and [base+size, PHYS_ADDR_MAX) from memblock.reserved. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewer right: the warning is printed only when no memory is registered; size==0 returns silently (memblock.c:1892-1898). Old prose attributed the warning to size zero.

name: check_sysctl_memfd_noexec
prose: Static function check_sysctl_memfd_noexec(flags) on memfd_create flags. Without CONFIG_SYSCTL it does nothing and returns 0. With CONFIG_SYSCTL it reads the pid namespace's memfd_noexec scope (sysctl). If neither MFD_EXEC nor MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL is set in *flags, it sets MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL when sysctl >= MEMFD_NOEXEC_SCOPE_NOEXEC_SEAL and MFD_EXEC otherwise; if either flag is already set, *flags is not changed by this step. Then, if MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL is not set in *flags (after the step above) and sysctl >= MEMFD_NOEXEC_SCOPE_NOEXEC_ENFORCED, it logs a rate-limited error and returns -EACCES (any flag change from the first step stays in *flags). In every other case it returns 0. In particular, an enforced scope with MFD_EXEC and MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL both set returns 0, and an enforced scope with neither flag set gets MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL added and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 right: -EACCES requires MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL clear, not merely MFD_EXEC set (memfd.c:358). Reviewers 1 and 2 right too: flags unchanged when a mode flag is already set or CONFIG_SYSCTL is off; the first step runs before the enforcement test (351-358). Note old prose said *flags unchanged on -EACCES, but the first step may already have added MFD_EXEC.

name: do_wp_page
prose: Static function do_wp_page(vmf) for a write-protect fault, entered with the PTE mapped and vmf->ptl held (declared __releases(vmf->ptl)); the caller holds the mmap_lock for read or, for a per-VMA-lock fault (FAULT_FLAG_VMA_LOCK), the VMA read lock. If the fault is not an unshare and the PTE carries a userfaultfd write-protect bit: when the vma is not in async uffd-wp mode it unmaps and unlocks the PTE and returns handle_userfault(vmf, VM_UFFD_WP) (which may drop the mmap_lock and return VM_FAULT_RETRY); in async mode it clears the uffd-wp bit in the PTE and in vmf->orig_pte and continues. If userfaultfd write-protect is active on the vma and a TLB flush is pending it flushes the page. It then looks up vmf->page with vm_normal_page. Shared vma (VM_SHARED or VM_MAYSHARE): with no page or an fsdax page it clears vmf->page and returns wp_pfn_shared(vmf); otherwise it returns wp_page_shared(vmf, folio). Both callees unmap and unlock the PTE, and may call ->pfn_mkwrite or ->page_mkwrite; they can return 0 without making the PTE writable (for example when do_page_mkwrite returns 0), VM_FAULT_RETRY (vmf_can_call_fault ends the per-VMA lock read when the vma has no ->map_pages), or error/NOPAGE bits from the callbacks and finish_mkwrite_fault. Private vma: if the folio is anonymous and either the page is already PageAnonExclusive or wp_can_reuse_anon_folio allows reuse, it marks the page anon-exclusive and then, for an unshare fault, unmaps and unlocks the PTE and returns 0; otherwise calls wp_page_reuse and returns 0. In all other cases it takes a folio reference when there is a folio, unmaps and unlocks the PTE, counts COW_KSM for a KSM folio, and returns wp_page_copy(vmf). On every path the PTE is unmapped and unlocked before return. So the result is 0 on the reuse paths, or whatever handle_userfault, wp_pfn_shared, wp_page_shared or wp_page_copy return.
note: Reviewer 1 right (error returns from callees, handle_userfault may drop mmap_lock: memory.c:4075). Reviewer 2 right that precondition must allow the per-VMA lock, and RETRY from vmf_can_call_fault drops the VMA lock (memory.c:3618), so the old 'lock still held' claim was wrong. Reviewer 3 right: wp_page_shared returns 0 from do_page_mkwrite without reuse/copy (3905-3908).

name: do_swap_page
prose: Function do_swap_page(vmf) in mm/memory.c, handling a fault on a non-present PTE that holds a swap or special entry; the slice cut its head. The PTE lock is not held on entry. If pte_unmap_same reports the PTE changed it returns 0. For non-swap entries: a migration entry waits and returns 0; a device-exclusive entry returns remove_device_exclusive_entry(vmf); a device-private entry returns VM_FAULT_RETRY (after vma_end_read) under FAULT_FLAG_VMA_LOCK, otherwise locks the PTE and returns 0 if it changed, else returns the pgmap ->migrate_to_ram result when the page trylock succeeds, or waits and returns 0 when it does not; a hwpoison entry returns VM_FAULT_HWPOISON; a PTE marker returns handle_pte_marker(vmf); any other entry logs print_bad_pte and returns VM_FAULT_SIGBUS. For a swap entry it takes a swap-device reference (get_swap_device; returns 0 if the device is gone), looks in the swap cache, and otherwise either allocates a folio and reads it directly (synchronous-IO swap with count 1) or calls swapin_readahead. If swapcache_prepare fails in the direct path it sleeps briefly, releases the new folio and returns 0 (so the fault is retried). If no folio could be obtained, it re-takes the PTE lock and returns VM_FAULT_OOM only when the PTE is unchanged, otherwise returns 0. A folio read from swap makes the result VM_FAULT_MAJOR. The folio lock is taken with folio_lock_or_retry; VM_FAULT_RETRY is returned if that asks for a retry. Later failures: folio not matching the swap entry returns ret unchanged (0 or MAJOR); a hwpoisoned swapcache page, or ksm_might_need_to_copy returning -EHWPOISON, returns VM_FAULT_HWPOISON; ksm_might_need_to_copy returning NULL returns VM_FAULT_OOM; after re-taking the PTE lock a changed PTE returns ret unchanged and a folio that is not uptodate returns VM_FAULT_SIGBUS, in both cases unlocking the PTE. On success it installs the PTE(s) (possibly for the whole large folio), frees the swap entries (swap_free_nr), adjusts MM_ANONPAGES and MM_SWAPENTS, sets up rmap, unlocks the folio and the swapcache folio when a KSM copy was used, and drops the swapcache reference; if FAULT_FLAG_WRITE is still set it ORs in do_wp_page(vmf) and keeps only the VM_FAULT_ERROR bits if an error was reported, else it updates the MMU cache and unlocks the PTE. Returns 0 or VM_FAULT_MAJOR (possibly with do_wp_page bits). Before returning on the swap-entry paths it clears the swap-cache pin if it set one (swapcache_clear and wake-up) and drops the swap device reference.
note: Slice cut head (do_swap_page at memory.c:4596). Reviewer right: swapcache_prepare failure (4703-4711, out_page with ret 0) and a concurrently changed PTE (4741-4744, 4814-4815) do not return VM_FAULT_OOM; OOM is returned only when the PTE is unchanged after allocation fails, or when ksm_might_need_to_copy returns NULL (4784-4787). The old prose also overstated 'on every path ... dropped'.

name: mhp_get_default_online_type
prose: Returns the cached default memory-hotplug online type mhp_default_online_type (a static int initialised to -1). If the cached value is already non-negative it returns it. Otherwise it sets the cache from the build configuration: MMOP_OFFLINE for CONFIG_MHP_DEFAULT_ONLINE_TYPE_OFFLINE, MMOP_ONLINE, MMOP_ONLINE_KERNEL or MMOP_ONLINE_MOVABLE for the matching ONLINE_* option, and MMOP_OFFLINE if none of those options is enabled, and returns the new value. MMOP_OFFLINE is 0, so after the first call the cache is non-negative and later calls return it directly. Takes no lock; the cache update is a plain store.
note: Old prose said MMOP_OFFLINE is -1 and the initialization repeats on every call: wrong, enum mmop has MMOP_OFFLINE = 0 (include/linux/memory_hotplug.h:22), so only the -1 initial value triggers initialization (memory_hotplug.c:223-227). Reviewer 1's claim that it can return MMOP_OFFLINE (-1) is wrong for the same reason.

name: offline_pages
prose: Function offline_pages(start_pfn, nr_pages, zone, group); the caller must hold mem_hotplug_lock in write mode. Early failures with nothing changed: -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if nr_pages is 0, start_pfn is not pageblock-aligned or start_pfn+nr_pages is not PAGES_PER_SECTION-aligned; -EINVAL (no warning, only a pr_debug message) if the system-RAM pages counted in the range differ from nr_pages (holes); -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if the first or last page of the range is not in zone. Otherwise it disables the zone's pcplists and the LRU caches and calls start_isolate_page_range; a non-zero result is returned after re-enabling them. If nr_pages is at least the node's present pages it notifies NODE_REMOVING_LAST_MEMORY, and it then notifies MEM_GOING_OFFLINE; an error from either is returned (as an errno) after undoing the isolation, sending the cancel notifications and re-enabling the caches and pcplists. It then loops: it checks signal_pending (returns -EINTR through the same undo path), repeatedly calls scan_movable_pages and do_migrate_range, and if scan_movable_pages returns any error other than -ENOENT (the unmovable-page case) that error is returned through the undo path; it then calls dissolve_free_hugetlb_folios (error returned through the undo path) and test_pages_isolated; a non-zero test_pages_isolated result does not fail the call, the whole loop is repeated. When the loop ends it marks the sections offline and removes the free pages from the buddy (__offline_isolated_pages), fixes up nr_isolate_pageblock under zone->lock, re-enables LRU caches and pcplists, adjusts managed and present page counts, updates watermarks, node state (clearing N_NORMAL_MEMORY / N_MEMORY when the node has none left), possibly resets the zone and rebuilds zonelists, stops kcompactd/kswapd and notifies NODE_REMOVED_LAST_MEMORY when the node became memoryless, sends MEM_OFFLINE, calls remove_pfn_range_from_zone and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 2 right (the hole case has no WARN_ON_ONCE, memory_hotplug.c:1956-1960). Reviewer 15 right: unmovable-page failure returns scan_movable_pages' error (2037-2039), which the old list omitted; also test_pages_isolated errors are retried, not returned (2053-2056), so the old prose listing it as a propagated error was wrong. Reviewers 1 and old contract points: precondition/postcondition split is consistent in the new text.

name: mpol_misplaced
prose: Function mpol_misplaced(folio, vmf, addr) returns the node from which a replacement folio should be allocated, or NUMA_NO_NODE when no migration is wanted. It asserts (lockdep) that vmf->ptl is held, and gets the vma policy with get_vma_policy; the policy reference is released with mpol_cond_put on the single exit path. If the policy does not have MPOL_F_MOF it returns NUMA_NO_NODE immediately, before looking at the policy mode. Otherwise it chooses a target node polnid by mode: MPOL_INTERLEAVE and MPOL_WEIGHTED_INTERLEAVE use the interleave helpers; MPOL_PREFERRED returns NUMA_NO_NODE if the folio's node is in the policy nodes, else uses the first policy node; MPOL_LOCAL uses the current node; MPOL_BIND and MPOL_PREFERRED_MANY with MPOL_F_MORON proceed only if the current node is in the policy nodes (else NUMA_NO_NODE), and without MPOL_F_MORON return NUMA_NO_NODE if the folio's node is in the policy nodes, else take the node of the first zone of the current node's zonelist restricted to the policy nodes; any other mode value calls BUG(), reachable only with MPOL_F_MOF set. Then, if MPOL_F_MORON is set, polnid becomes the current node and should_numa_migrate_memory must approve, otherwise NUMA_NO_NODE is returned. Finally it returns polnid if it differs from the folio's current node and NUMA_NO_NODE if it is equal.
note: Reviewer 2 right (MOF early return, mempolicy.c:2925-2926). Reviewer 3 right: BUG() only after the MOF check. Reviewer 1: NUMA_NO_NODE also results from the other paths (curnid==polnid, MORON decline); its specific claim about 'no allowed nodes' is not supported: zonelist_node_idx() is zone_to_nid(z->zone) with no NULL handling (mmzone.h:1721-1724), and the code comment says no allowed nodes should be treated as not misplaced; I did not claim a NO_NODE return for that case.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(brk, unsigned long, brk)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_brk(brk), the brk system call in mm/mmap.c; the slice's name do_brk_syscall does not exist. It takes mmap_write_lock_killable(mm) and returns -EINTR (as the unsigned long result) if that fails. Otherwise origbrk = mm->brk and min_brk = mm->start_brk (or mm->end_data under CONFIG_COMPAT_BRK when the task's brk is not randomized). Failure paths (go to out): brk below min_brk; check_data_rlimit failure; for shrinking, no VMA found or the found VMA starts at or after the old page-aligned break, or do_vmi_align_munmap fails; for growing, check_brk_limits fails, the next VMA is within the stack guard gap of the new area, or do_brk_flags returns negative. On failure mm->brk is reset to origbrk, the mmap write lock is released and origbrk is returned. Success paths: if the page-aligned old and new breaks are equal, mm->brk = brk and the write lock is released; shrinking (brk <= mm->brk) sets mm->brk = brk and calls do_vmi_align_munmap with unlock=true, which releases the lock on success; growing sets mm->brk = brk after do_brk_flags and releases the lock. In all success cases userfaultfd_unmap_complete runs, and mm_populate(oldbrk, newbrk-oldbrk) is called when the grow path set populate (mm->def_flags has VM_LOCKED); it returns brk.
note: Name was do_brk_syscall, which is not in mmap.c; the function is SYSCALL_DEFINE1(brk, ...) at mmap.c:115. Old prose mostly right; tightened the failure list and populate condition (populate is only set on the grow path, 198-199). No reviewer claim besides the mechanical name one.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(munmap, unsigned long, addr, size_t, len)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_munmap(addr, len) (entry sys_munmap). It replaces addr with untagged_addr(addr) and returns __vm_munmap(addr, len, true). __vm_munmap takes the current mm's mmap write lock (returning -EINTR if that is interrupted by a fatal signal), calls do_vmi_munmap and, when the unmap fails, releases the lock itself (on success with unlock=true the lock has already been released inside do_vmi_munmap), then runs userfaultfd_unmap_complete; so the result is 0 or the negative errno from do_vmi_munmap or -EINTR.
note: Name changed to the macro head (mmap.c:1077). Checked against __vm_munmap (mm/vma.c:3216-3232); old prose 'mmap lock released' kept but attributed to the callee.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(remap_file_pages, unsigned long, start, unsigned long, size, unsigned long, prot, unsigned long, pgoff, unsigned long, flags)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_remap_file_pages(start, size, prot, pgoff, flags), an emulation of the deprecated system call; it logs a pr_warn_once on first use. It returns -EINVAL at once (no lock taken) if prot is non-zero, if after masking start and size with PAGE_MASK start+size <= start, or if pgoff + (size >> PAGE_SHIFT) wraps. It then takes mmap_read_lock_killable (returning -EINTR on interruption), looks up the VMA at start, and if there is none or it is not VM_SHARED releases the lock and returns -EINVAL. It derives prot and flags from the VMA, saves its vm_flags, takes a reference on its file, drops the read lock, and calls security_mmap_file; a non-zero result is returned after fput. It then takes mmap_write_lock_killable (-EINTR after fput on failure), looks up the VMA at start again and fails with -EINVAL if there is none or its vm_flags or vm_file differ from the saved values, or if the range extends past that VMA and the following VMAs are not contiguous with the same vm_file and vm_flags up to start+size. Otherwise it returns the result of do_mmap(...) after mapping the range: 0 on success or the error value from do_mmap. Cleanup after the write lock was taken: the write lock is released and the file reference dropped with fput on every path; mm_populate(ret, populate) is called if do_mmap set populate to non-zero. On every path where a reference was taken it is dropped with fput.
note: Name changed to the macro head (mmap.c:1087). The old prose put checks as preconditions although the code rejects them with -EINVAL; rewritten as behaviour. fput/locks verified on all returns (1124-1125, 1146, 1154, 1197-1198).

name: dup_mmap
prose: Function dup_mmap(mm, oldmm) (declared __latent_entropy int), which copies the address space of oldmm into the new mm; the slice cut its head. It first calls mmap_write_lock_killable(oldmm) and returns -EINTR if that fails, before anything else happens. Otherwise it takes the nested write lock on mm, copies the VM counters, and duplicates the maple tree with __mt_dup; if that fails it goes to out with its error and without marking mm unstable. It then walks the VMAs: VM_DONTCOPY VMAs are cleared from the child's tree; for others it checks for a fatal signal (-EINTR), accounts memory, duplicates the VMA and its policy, runs dup_userfaultfd, forks the anon_vma (or clears it for VM_WIPEONFORK), links the VMA, calls vm_ops->open, adds file mappings to the i_mmap tree and calls copy_page_range unless VM_WIPEONFORK. After the loop it calls arch_dup_mmap. Failures give -ENOMEM (memory accounting, vm_area_dup, vma_dup_policy, dup_userfaultfd and anon_vma_fork all end at labels that set -ENOMEM), -EINTR for a pending fatal signal, or the error from vma_iter_clear_gfp, copy_page_range or arch_dup_mmap. On success it marks the tree in-RCU, calls ksm_fork and khugepaged_fork, releases both write locks, flushes the TLB of oldmm, calls dup_userfaultfd_complete and returns 0. On a failure after the tree was duplicated it stores XA_ZERO_ENTRY over the VMA reached (and sets MMF_OOM_SKIP) only if mpnt is non-NULL, sets MMF_UNSTABLE, releases both locks, flushes oldmm's TLB, calls dup_userfaultfd_fail and returns the error.
note: Slice cut head (dup_mmap at mmap.c:1719). Reviewer right on both points: the -EINTR return at 1727-1728 skips the unlock and flush; XA_ZERO_ENTRY only when mpnt is non-NULL (1858-1863); additionally the __mt_dup failure path skips MMF_UNSTABLE (1746-1747, 1871).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(mprotect, unsigned long, start, size_t, len, unsigned long, prot)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_mprotect(start, len, prot) (entry sys_mprotect): returns do_mprotect_pkey(start, len, prot, -1), where -1 means no protection key. It holds no lock itself. Behaviour of do_mprotect_pkey(start, len, prot, pkey), to which the syscall forwards: Checks before the lock: start is replaced with untagged_addr(start); returns -EINVAL if both PROT_GROWSDOWN and PROT_GROWSUP are set, or if start is not page-aligned; returns 0 if len is 0; len is page-aligned and if end = start+len is not above start it returns -ENOMEM; returns -EINVAL if arch_validate_prot rejects prot. It then takes mmap_write_lock_killable on current->mm and returns -EINTR if that fails. With the lock held: (because pkey is -1 no pkey check is made) it finds the first VMA at or after start (-ENOMEM if none); with PROT_GROWSDOWN it returns -ENOMEM if that VMA starts at or after end, moves start down to the VMA start and gives -EINVAL if the VMA lacks VM_GROWSDOWN; otherwise it gives -ENOMEM if the VMA starts after start, and with PROT_GROWSUP moves end up to the VMA end and gives -EINVAL if it lacks VM_GROWSUP. It then walks the VMAs in [start, end): a gap gives -ENOMEM; for each VMA it computes the new flags (adding PROT_EXEC if READ_IMPLIES_EXEC applies and the VMA has VM_MAYEXEC), and breaks with -EACCES if the new access flags exceed the VM_MAY flags or map_deny_write_exec rejects the change, -EINVAL if arch_validate_flags rejects them, or the error from security_file_mprotect, the VMA's mprotect method, or mprotect_fixup (which includes its own errors such as -ENOMEM). After the loop, if no error occurred but the walk did not reach end, the result is -ENOMEM. The mmap write lock is released on every return that follows its acquisition, and the result is 0 or the negative errno above. VMAs modified before a failure stay modified; this function does not undo them.
note: Old prose described do_mprotect_pkey as if it were the syscall body (mprotect.c:1008-1012); rewritten to say it forwards. Reviewer (round 2) right that nothing here undoes earlier VMA updates (loop break at 939-992 leaves them); the old claim that charged memory 'remains accounted' cannot be pointed to a line in this function, so it was dropped. Name changed to the macro head.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(pkey_mprotect, unsigned long, start, size_t, len, unsigned long, prot, int, pkey)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_pkey_mprotect(start, len, prot, pkey), compiled only when CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_PKEYS is set: returns do_mprotect_pkey(start, len, prot, pkey). It holds no lock itself. Behaviour of do_mprotect_pkey(start, len, prot, pkey), to which the syscall forwards: Checks before the lock: start is replaced with untagged_addr(start); returns -EINVAL if both PROT_GROWSDOWN and PROT_GROWSUP are set, or if start is not page-aligned; returns 0 if len is 0; len is page-aligned and if end = start+len is not above start it returns -ENOMEM; returns -EINVAL if arch_validate_prot rejects prot. It then takes mmap_write_lock_killable on current->mm and returns -EINTR if that fails. With the lock held: if pkey is not -1 and is not allocated in current->mm it returns -EINVAL; it finds the first VMA at or after start (-ENOMEM if none); with PROT_GROWSDOWN it returns -ENOMEM if that VMA starts at or after end, moves start down to the VMA start and gives -EINVAL if the VMA lacks VM_GROWSDOWN; otherwise it gives -ENOMEM if the VMA starts after start, and with PROT_GROWSUP moves end up to the VMA end and gives -EINVAL if it lacks VM_GROWSUP. It then walks the VMAs in [start, end): a gap gives -ENOMEM; for each VMA it computes the new flags (adding PROT_EXEC if READ_IMPLIES_EXEC applies and the VMA has VM_MAYEXEC), and breaks with -EACCES if the new access flags exceed the VM_MAY flags or map_deny_write_exec rejects the change, -EINVAL if arch_validate_flags rejects them, or the error from security_file_mprotect, the VMA's mprotect method, or mprotect_fixup (which includes its own errors such as -ENOMEM). After the loop, if no error occurred but the walk did not reach end, the result is -ENOMEM. The mmap write lock is released on every return that follows its acquisition, and the result is 0 or the negative errno above. VMAs modified before a failure stay modified; this function does not undo them.
note: Same as mprotect: syscall body only forwards (mprotect.c:1016-1019); old claim about retained memory accounting dropped. Name changed to the macro head.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(mseal, unsigned long, start, size_t, len, unsigned long, flags)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_mseal(start, len, flags) (entry sys_mseal): returns do_mseal(start, len, flags). Behaviour of do_mseal: returns -EINVAL if flags is non-zero; start is replaced by untagged_addr(start) and -EINVAL is returned if it is not page-aligned; len is rounded up to a page multiple and -EINVAL is returned if a non-zero len rounds to zero or if start+len overflows; returns 0 if the resulting range is empty. Then it takes mmap_write_lock_killable (-EINTR if that fails), returns -ENOMEM if range_contains_unmapped finds a gap, otherwise calls mseal_apply, which sets VM_SEALED on each VMA in the range using vma_modify_flags (an error from that call, such as a split or merge failure, is returned; VMAs sealed before the failure stay sealed) and returns 0 when all VMAs are processed. The mmap write lock is released on every return after it was acquired; the early -EINVAL and 0 returns happen before the lock is taken.
note: Reviewer right that the old contract's precondition excluded the overflow / round-to-zero -EINVAL paths. A contract is not appropriate here (the function touches the current mm), so it is left empty. Name changed to the macro head (mseal.c:187). Old claim 'lock always released' corrected: early returns precede the lock.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(mmap_pgoff, unsigned long, addr, unsigned long, len, unsigned long, prot, unsigned long, flags, unsigned long, fd, unsigned long, pgoff)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_mmap_pgoff(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, pgoff) in the nommu build (mm/nommu.c). Its body returns ksys_mmap_pgoff(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, pgoff) and does nothing else. ksys_mmap_pgoff (nommu version) calls audit_mmap_fd; if MAP_ANONYMOUS is not set it looks the file up with fget(fd) and returns -EBADF if there is none; it then returns vm_mmap_pgoff(file, ...) and calls fput on the file when one was taken. So the syscall's result is -EBADF for an unresolvable fd when MAP_ANONYMOUS is clear, or whatever vm_mmap_pgoff returns (a mapped address or a negative errno).
note: Slice is the nommu.c version (nommu.c:1271-1276), not mmap.c's; the function ksys_mmap_pgoff there has no hugetlb handling. Reviewer 2: not contradicted by the code, but unproven; the new prose says -EBADF comes from fget here and that vm_mmap_pgoff results are passed through unchanged. Name changed to the macro head.

name: gfp_to_alloc_flags_cma
prose: Static inline function gfp_to_alloc_flags_cma(gfp_mask, alloc_flags); it must be called after current_gfp_context() has adjusted gfp_mask. It returns alloc_flags unchanged unless CONFIG_CMA is enabled and gfp_migratetype(gfp_mask) equals MIGRATE_MOVABLE, in which case it returns alloc_flags with ALLOC_CMA set. gfp_migratetype reads the global page_group_by_mobility_disabled (which makes it return MIGRATE_UNMOVABLE) and otherwise derives the migratetype from the __GFP_MOVABLE and __GFP_RECLAIMABLE bits of gfp_mask; no other bits of alloc_flags are changed and no lock or reference is taken.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the function never tests __GFP_HIGHATOMIC (page_alloc.c:3759-3767); in gfp_migratetype that value would only arise as MIGRATE_HIGHATOMIC when both MOVABLE and RECLAIMABLE bits are set. Reviewer 1 right that MIGRATE_MOVABLE is 1 not 2. No contract given since it depends on a global.

name: __alloc_pages_slowpath
prose: Static function __alloc_pages_slowpath(gfp_mask, order, ac), the slow path of the page allocator, entered after the fast path failed; the slice started in the middle of its body. It returns a struct page pointer or NULL. For __GFP_NOFAIL it first issues WARN_ON_ONCE for order > 1, for missing __GFP_DIRECT_RECLAIM and for PF_MEMALLOC. Each pass (restart) recomputes alloc_flags and the preferred zoneref; it goes to nopage if no zone is usable or the cpuset configuration is insane for a __GFP_HARDWALL request. It wakes kswapd when ALLOC_KSWAPD is set, tries get_page_from_freelist, then, for costly or non-movable high-order allocations that may reclaim and compact, tries direct compaction first; a costly __GFP_NORETRY allocation goes to nopage when compaction was skipped or deferred, or when __GFP_THISNODE is set. In the retry loop it restarts if the cpuset or zonelist changed, applies memory-reserve flags and resets the nodemask when memory policies may be ignored, and retries get_page_from_freelist. It goes to nopage if the caller cannot direct-reclaim, if PF_MEMALLOC is set, after failed direct reclaim and compaction when __GFP_NORETRY is set, for costly orders without compaction and __GFP_RETRY_MAYFAIL, when the retry heuristics (should_reclaim_retry, should_compact_retry) decline and the OOM killer attempt gives no page, for an OOM victim restricted by ALLOC_OOM or __GFP_NOMEMALLOC, or when the OOM killer made no progress. If the OOM killer made progress it retries. At nopage a cpuset or zonelist change restarts the function. With __GFP_NOFAIL and direct reclaim allowed it tries a reserve-limited fallback allocation (ALLOC_MIN_RESERVE) and otherwise loops back to retry, so it does not return NULL in that case; with __GFP_NOFAIL but no direct reclaim it goes to fail. Every other path reaching nopage proceeds to fail, which calls warn_alloc and returns NULL (page is NULL). Success paths return the page obtained from the freelist, direct reclaim, compaction, OOM or fallback attempt.
note: Slice cut the head: the code is __alloc_pages_slowpath (page_alloc.c:4729), not __alloc_pages. Reviewer right: NULL is returned after warn_alloc from the early nopage paths (no usable zone, PF_MEMALLOC, __GFP_NORETRY, no direct reclaim, costly-order checks, 4818-4890, 5014-5030), not only after reclaim, compaction and OOM all fail. Old claim 'charged to the caller' is not in this function and was dropped.

name: folio_walk_start
prose: Function folio_walk_start(fw, vma, addr, flags) walks the page tables of vma->vm_mm for addr and returns the folio mapped there, or NULL; the slice contained only its tail. The caller must hold the mm's mmap lock (checked with mmap_assert_locked); the function calls vma_pgtable_walk_begin first. If addr is outside the vma (WARN_ON_ONCE) or any page-table level is empty or bad it ends the walk and returns NULL. At PUD and PMD level, huge-leaf (or non-present) entries are examined under the page-table lock; a present leaf with a normal page is found, a huge zero PMD is found only if FW_ZEROPAGE is in flags, a PMD migration entry only if FW_MIGRATION is in flags; otherwise the lock is released and NULL returned (a PUD migration entry is not supported). At PTE level it maps and locks the PTE; a present PTE with a normal page is found, the zero page is found only with FW_ZEROPAGE, a migration entry only with FW_MIGRATION; any other PTE unmaps and unlocks it and returns NULL. On success it returns page_folio(page) with fw->level and the level's pointer and value recorded, fw->ptl set to the held lock, and the lock and page-table walk left active for the caller to finish with folio_walk_end. fw->page is the found page plus the offset of addr within the entry for normal pages, and NULL for zero-page and migration results. On failure it returns NULL with no page-table lock held and the walk ended.
note: Slice cut the head (function begins at pagewalk.c:898, slice at 1015). Reviewer right: flags is not required to be non-empty: flags == 0 still returns normal-page folios (1015-1018), only the zero page and migration cases depend on FW_ZEROPAGE and FW_MIGRATION.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(readahead, int, fd, loff_t, offset, size_t, count)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_readahead(fd, offset, count) (entry sys_readahead): its body returns ksys_readahead(fd, offset, count) and nothing else. ksys_readahead looks up fd (CLASS(fd), released at scope exit) and returns -EBADF if the descriptor is empty or the file is not open for reading; returns -EINVAL if the file has no f_mapping or no a_ops, if the inode is neither a regular file nor a block device, or if the inode is an anonymous file; otherwise it returns vfs_fadvise(file, offset, count, POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED), i.e. the file's f_op->fadvise result if defined or generic_fadvise's result, which is 0 or a negative errno. No lock or reference is left held after the call.
note: Name changed to the macro head (readahead.c:733). Old prose checked against ksys_readahead at readahead.c:701-731 and is right; tightened. Slice did not contain the function (name outside slice).

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(readahead, int, fd, compat_arg_u64_dual(offset), size_t, count)
prose: Generated compat function (entry compat_sys_readahead / __x64_compat_sys_readahead), compiled only when CONFIG_COMPAT and __ARCH_WANT_COMPAT_READAHEAD are set. It glues the two 32-bit halves of offset into a 64-bit value with compat_arg_u64_glue and returns ksys_readahead(fd, glued offset, count). ksys_readahead returns -EBADF for an empty fd or a file not open for reading, -EINVAL for a file without f_mapping or a_ops, for an inode that is neither regular nor a block device, or for an anonymous file, and otherwise vfs_fadvise(..., POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED), which is 0 or a negative errno. No lock or reference is left held after the call.
note: Name changed to the macro head (readahead.c:739). Old prose confirmed against ksys_readahead.

name: try_to_migrate_one
prose: Static function try_to_migrate_one(folio, vma, address, arg), an rmap-walk callback where arg is the ttu_flags value; it is not try_to_unmap_one (the slice is the tail of try_to_migrate_one in mm/rmap.c). It returns true unless one of the aborting cases below occurs, in which case it returns false. It sets up an mmu_notifier invalidation range (widened for possible hugetlb PMD sharing) and starts it, then iterates page_vma_mapped_walk. For a PMD-mapped entry (no pte): with TTU_SPLIT_HUGE_PMD set it splits the PMD, clears that flag and restarts the walk; otherwise (only when CONFIG_ARCH_ENABLE_THP_MIGRATION is set) it installs a PMD migration entry with set_pmd_migration_entry, and if that fails it ends the walk and returns false. For a PTE it reads the current PTE (device-exclusive style swap PTEs are also handled) and clears it. A hugetlb folio that is not anonymous requires TTU_RMAP_LOCKED (VM_BUG_ON); if hugetlb_vma_trylock_write fails it ends the walk and returns false, and if huge_pmd_unshare succeeds the walk ends with the PMD table removed (the result stays true, and no folio_put is done for that step). Otherwise the PTE is cleared with flush (or deferred flush) and the dirty state moved to the folio. Replacement: a hwpoisoned subpage gets a hwpoison swap entry; a present PTE marked unused is discarded if no userfaultfd is armed; otherwise arch_unmap_one is called (failure restores the PTE and returns false) and, for an anon-exclusive page, folio_try_share_anon_rmap_pte / hugetlb_try_share_anon_rmap must succeed (failure restores the PTE and returns false). Then a writable, exclusive-readable or readable migration entry is installed, carrying young, dirty, soft-dirty and uffd-wp bits. After replacing a PTE it removes the rmap for the subpage, drains the local mlock cache for VM_LOCKED vmas and drops one folio reference with folio_put. The mmu_notifier range is ended on all paths and the function returns ret.
note: Slice cut the head and the real function is try_to_migrate_one (rmap.c:2314), not try_to_unmap_one: the old prose described mlock, swapbacked/MADV_FREE and swap_duplicate cases that exist only in try_to_unmap_one. Reviewer right that set_pmd_migration_entry failure returns false (rmap.c:2377-2381); old prose also missed the arch_unmap_one and anon-share failures' precise handling.

name: shmem_get_unmapped_area
prose: Function shmem_get_unmapped_area(file, uaddr, len, pgoff, flags) chooses an address for a shmem mapping (file may be NULL for a shared anonymous object). It returns -ENOMEM if len > TASK_SIZE. Otherwise it calls mm_get_unmapped_area for the request and keeps that address (addr) as the default result. It returns addr unchanged (which may be an error value) in each of these cases: CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE is off; addr is an error value, is not page-aligned, or is above TASK_SIZE - len; shmem_huge is SHMEM_HUGE_DENY; MAP_FIXED is set; addr equals the hint uaddr; when shmem_huge is not SHMEM_HUGE_FORCE, the filesystem's huge setting is SHMEM_HUGE_NEVER and no anonymous mTHP order applies (and for file == NULL, when shm_mnt is an error pointer); len is smaller than the huge-page size; the file offset within a huge page is non-zero and offset+len is below twice the huge-page size; addr already has the same offset within a huge page as the file offset; the inflated request (len plus huge-page size minus PAGE_SIZE) exceeds TASK_SIZE or overflows, mm_get_unmapped_area for it fails or returns an unaligned address, or the adjusted address would lie above TASK_SIZE - len. Otherwise it returns the inflated-request address shifted so that its offset within a huge page equals the file offset, leaving at least len bytes below TASK_SIZE. The huge-page size is HPAGE_PMD_SIZE, or for anonymous shmem (file == NULL) the size of the highest enabled mTHP order when there is one. Takes no lock itself.
note: Reviewer right: addr is returned unchanged when it is already at the huge-page offset (shmem.c:2874-2875) and when addr == uaddr (2826-2827), which the old prose did not list precisely. Old 'offset alignment unsuitable' wording replaced by the exact conditions. Slice head was cut (function at shmem.c:2790).

name: kmem_cache_flags
prose: The !CONFIG_SLUB_DEBUG variant of kmem_cache_flags(flags, name): returns flags unchanged and ignores name; it has no side effects. (With CONFIG_SLUB_DEBUG a different function of the same name applies the slub_debug options.)
note: 'kmem_cache_flags_no_debug' is not a real name; the code is the stub kmem_cache_flags at slub.c:2014-2017 in the #else branch. Fixed rather than dropped since it is a function.

name: #define STAT_ATTR(si, text)
prose: Macro that generates two static sysfs handlers for one slab statistic and registers them with SLAB_ATTR(text). The generated text_show(s, buf) returns show_stat(s, buf, si). The generated text_store(s, buf, length) returns -EINVAL without changing any statistic if buf[0] is not the character '0'; if buf[0] is '0' it calls clear_stat(s, si), which sets the si counter to 0 in the per-CPU slab data of every online CPU, and returns length. It reads buf[0] even when length is 0.
note: Reviewer right: the macro also defines text_show returning show_stat (slub.c:9418-9423), which the old text omitted. Name changed to the macro definition head.
